definition: HiGHS is open-source software to solve linear programming (LP), mixed-integer programming (MIP), and convex quadratic programming (QP) models.
details: Written in C++ and published under an MIT license, HiGHS provides programming interfaces to C, Python, Julia, Rust, R, JavaScript, Fortran, and C#. It has no external dependencies. A convenient thin wrapper to Python is available via the highspy PyPI package. HiGHS is also callable via NuGet. Although generally single-threaded, some solver components can utilize multi-core architectures and, from Version 1.10.0, can run its first order LP solver on NVIDIA GPUs. HiGHS is designed to solve large-scale models and exploits problem sparsity. Its performance relative to commercial and other open-source software is reviewed periodically using industry-standard benchmarks. The term HiGHS may also refer to both the underlying project and the small team leading the software development.

explainer.lead: HiGHS is open-source software for solving linear programming, mixed-integer programming, and convex quadratic programming models. It matters as a dependency-free, MIT-licensed solver with interfaces to many languages.

tiers.eli5: It's a free tool that takes a math problem about making the best choice under limits and finds the answer, and you can plug it into lots of different programming languages.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers call HiGHS from C, Python (via highspy), Julia, Rust, R, JavaScript, Fortran, or C#, and via NuGet. A pitfall is that it is generally single-threaded, though some components use multi-core and, from version 1.10.0, its first-order LP solver can run on NVIDIA GPUs.
tiers.paperLevel: HiGHS solves LP, MIP, and convex QP models; it is written in C++ under an MIT license, has no external dependencies, is generally single-threaded, and is designed to solve large-scale models.

explainer.example: A Python user installs highspy, defines an LP model, and calls HiGHS to solve it without adding any external dependencies.
